decks.name: LeetCode #46 - Permutations
decks.description: Generate all possible permutations of distinct integers

cards.question: Permutations: Given an array nums of distinct integers, return all the possible permutations. You can return the answer in any order.

solutions.name: Recursion
solutions.explanation: Build permutations recursively by inserting first element into all positions of permutations of remaining elements. Base case: empty array has one permutation (empty). Recursively get permutations of nums[1:], then for each permutation insert nums[0] at every possible position (0 to length). Creates n! permutations with O(n) insertion cost per permutation. O(n!*n²) time due to copying on each insertion. Simple but inefficient.

solutions.name: Iteration
solutions.explanation: Build permutations iteratively without recursion. Start with empty permutation. For each number, create new permutations by inserting it into every position of every existing permutation. After processing all numbers, have complete set of permutations. Avoids recursion overhead but still requires copying arrays for insertions. O(n!*n²) time complexity. Easier to understand than recursion.

solutions.name: Backtracking
solutions.explanation: Use backtracking with boolean array to track which elements are used. Build permutation element by element, trying each unused element at current position. When permutation complete (length equals n), add copy to result. Backtrack by removing element and marking as unused. Boolean array prevents using same element twice. O(n!*n) time for generating and copying n! permutations. Standard backtracking approach.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Bit Mask)
solutions.explanation: Optimize backtracking using bit mask instead of boolean array. Use integer where each bit represents whether element at that index is used. Check if element used with bitwise AND, mark as used with bitwise OR. More space efficient for tracking state. Each bit operation is O(1). Same time complexity O(n!*n) but slightly better constant factors. Elegant use of bit manipulation.

solutions.name: Backtracking (Optimal)
solutions.explanation: Most efficient backtracking using in-place swapping. No extra boolean array or bit mask needed. Fix element at each position by swapping with elements from current index onwards. Recursively permute remaining elements. Swap back to restore original order for next iteration. Generates permutations directly in input array. O(n!*n) time, O(n) space for recursion only. Best space efficiency among all approaches.
